findings.rootCause: LeoConfidenceModel robustness defects (b1). Critique reconciliation: (minor, wrapper add()) was decided explicitly in b1 and documented in LearnedOperatorCounts.add/LearnedMultiplierCounts.add. The wrapper's sums are execution-derived and valid without a prediction, while the model and the q-error recorders skip non-finite planned values. (minor, cross-sidecar epoch) The scenario is real: .leo surfaces load independently of the .operators sidecar that owns feedbackEpoch. It has no trust effect, because LmdbLeoSurfaceStats never calls decayedConfidence (lastEpoch is informational), and after b3 decayForMutation scales confidence by the commit's decay factor alone. The post-condition 'no decayed surface lastEpoch exceeds feedbackEpoch' holds structurally: decayPredicates/decayAll return true exactly when a surface was re-stamped, and then recordStoreMutation always assigns feedbackEpoch = nextEpoch. A test is used instead of a runtime assertion because no production behaviour depends on the invariant.
findings.change: Added the characterization test LmdbLeoSurfaceStatsTest#surfaceTrustIsIndependentOfTheFeedbackEpochTimeline. Surfaces recorded at epochs 10000+ (ahead of a reset feedbackEpoch) and at epochs 1+ produce identical estimates. Decaying them at an epoch behind (2048) and one ahead (20000) yields identical results: rows are preserved and confidence is exactly x0.5. This is test-only. The test passes on the existing code, as expected for a characterization of already-sound behaviour, so no failing pre-fix run exists.

findings.rootCause: Flat per-commit decay (b3). Critique major (the stamp delta is the wrong numerator) is addressed: the numerator is the sink's count of approved and deprecated statements (mutatedStatementsInTransaction), never the journal sequence. The denominator is the O(1) mdb_stat count. UNKNOWN falls back to the flat floor. bR re-audited the counting sites for double counting: approve->addStatement (+1), approveBuffered->flushPendingApproves(n) (+n), approveAllBulk (flushes the pending buffer, which counts itself, then +statementCount for the batch), approveAll (+size) and per-quad removal (+1). The paths are disjoint. The semantic-regression risk (bulk load in OFF mode) is covered by LmdbCommitMutationExtentTest#largeTransactionWithTheFrontierEstimatorOffCountsEveryStatement.

crossWpNotes: wp3 (critique missedFindings): the PackedPlanCache context (LmdbCascadesOptimizer.cacheContext) is not keyed on executionSnapshotEpoch.isPresent(), while the pipeline cache is. wp3-b3's LmdbPlanAssumptions / committedSnapshotDependent work covers the adjacent data-revision tier. wp6's publication gate lives on the per-query statistics, not on the cached plan, so a cached plan served to an overlay query still publishes nothing, and LmdbCascadesOptimizer annotates explain on every install.

wp4: the 3.7.5(c) guard-kernel telemetry contract is unchanged from b3. A telemetry-capable guard kernel must credit the counted statements to the right child's resultSizeActual/costFeedbackActualRows and to the join's right-row counters, and keep the statementCount<0 fallback and duplicate-context multiset semantics (JoinGuardKernelTrackingTest). MinusQueryEvaluationStepTest spill-file reds under the workspace java.io.tmpdir override are also wp4's.

wp5: this WP changes the PERSIST_VERSION of the shared .operators sidecar, which also discards the serialized FrontierLearningModel once. Coordinate so the bump happens only once. Post-commit Frontier bookkeeping failures now request a rebuild without marking the view stale (wp5's call).

Any benchmark or test that replays observations through a bare LmdbSailStore.getEvaluationStatistics() instance must call bindExecutionSnapshot(OptionalLong.of(...)) first. Otherwise nothing is published (fail closed).
